decision.question: Should the rs485_node generator add a 10 kOhm pull-down from the transceiver DE/RE net to GND?
decision.history: Raised during Phase 2 as a product call the owner kept. It keeps a rebooting node's driver off the bus (MCU pins float during reset) and could let the fail-safe claim stop citing D2 (MCU is a simplified model).

facts.fact: Topology U1 pin D2 drives the MAX485/MAX3485 DE and /RE pins together; PIN_DE_RE = 'D2'.
Claims on the design: rs485.failsafe_bias (monotone corners), driver_load, termination_dissipation, rail_current; D2 is cited per claim where the real MCU can reach it.
D2 register text: nothing in Phase 2 is scheduled to close it.
Added idle current when DE/RE is driven high: 5 V / 10 kOhm = 0.5 mA on Uno; 3.3 V / 10 kOhm = 0.33 mA on 3.3 V boards.
Changing the default output means rs485_node 0.2.0 -> version bump -> every signed RS-485 design returns 409 until re-patched.
M1 seeded-fault margin on this generator is thin: a 5% component fault moves V_AB by 2.3% against a 2% gate.
DE/RE default pin per board: Uno D2, ESP32-DevKitC GPIO4, Black Pill F411 PB0. None is a strapping pin (ESP32 straps are GPIO0, 2, 5, 12, 15; F411 strap is PB2/BOOT1) and none is reserved.

Stated assumption, not datasheet-verified: during MCU reset the GPIO driving DE/RE is a high-impedance input, and the MAX485/MAX3485 DE and /RE inputs are not specified to default to a safe state, so the driver may be enabled while the MCU reboots. The catalogue records only 'DE and RE tied, driven by one MCU GPIO; HIGH = transmit'. D7 (datasheet figures unverified) applies.

options.what_changes: Every new RS-485 design gets R4 10k DE/RE->GND; generator version bump.
options.benefits: Reboot contention removed by default; possible D2 drop on fail-safe claim.
options.costs: Signed RS-485 designs invalidated (409); one more part; 0.33-0.5 mA idle.

reversibility.how_to_undo: Remove R4 and bump again; signatures already invalidated stay invalidated.

options.what_changes: constraints.de_re_pulldown (default false) adds R4 when set.
options.benefits: Users on multi-drop buses get it; existing designs byte-identical.
options.costs: Another constraint to test and document.

reversibility.how_to_undo: Remove the constraint; no signed design changed.

options.what_changes: Nothing now; record trigger: first multi-drop bus or first flashed RS-485 board.
options.costs: Risk stays for anyone who flashes a node on a shared bus.

options.what_changes: Close the question.
options.costs: Loses the option if the risk is real.

unknowns: How many users will put a node on a shared multi-drop bus in Phase 2/3.

decision.question: Should the rs485_node generator add a 10 kOhm pull-down from the transceiver DE/RE net to GND?
decision.history: Raised during Phase 2 as a product call the owner kept. It keeps a rebooting node's driver off the bus (MCU pins float during reset) and could let the fail-safe claim stop citing D2 (MCU is a simplified model).

facts.fact: Topology U1 pin D2 drives the MAX485/MAX3485 DE and /RE pins together; PIN_DE_RE = 'D2'.
Claims on the design: rs485.failsafe_bias (monotone corners), driver_load, termination_dissipation, rail_current; D2 is cited per claim where the real MCU can reach it.
D2 register text: nothing in Phase 2 is scheduled to close it.
Added idle current when DE/RE is driven high: 5 V / 10 kOhm = 0.5 mA on Uno; 3.3 V / 10 kOhm = 0.33 mA on 3.3 V boards.
Changing the default output means rs485_node 0.2.0 -> version bump -> every signed RS-485 design returns 409 until re-patched.
M1 seeded-fault margin on this generator is thin: a 5% component fault moves V_AB by 2.3% against a 2% gate.
DE/RE default pin per board: Uno D2, ESP32-DevKitC GPIO4, Black Pill F411 PB0. None is a strapping pin (ESP32 straps are GPIO0, 2, 5, 12, 15; F411 strap is PB2/BOOT1) and none is reserved.

Stated assumption, not datasheet-verified: during MCU reset the GPIO driving DE/RE is a high-impedance input, and the MAX485/MAX3485 DE and /RE inputs are not specified to default to a safe state, so the driver may be enabled while the MCU reboots. The catalogue records only 'DE and RE tied, driven by one MCU GPIO; HIGH = transmit'. D7 (datasheet figures unverified) applies.

kind is not part of the sign-off hash.

kind lives inside CircuitIR.validation_coverage. same_design() drops validation_coverage before comparing, so changing kind does not change the circuit identity check, but it does change the full serialized CircuitIR.
